items.stem: A conglomerate argues it creates value by owning many unrelated businesses. Which test most directly challenges that claim?

options.text: The ownership (parenting) test: is the parent the best owner of each business?
options.rationale: Correct: the ownership test asks whether the parent, versus another owner, adds most value.

options.text: The five-forces test of industry attractiveness
options.rationale: Five forces assesses industries, not parenting logic.
Value-chain analysis is about a single business's advantage.
Break-even is a financial, not a corporate-ownership, test.

items.explanation: Correct: the ownership test asks whether the parent, versus another owner, adds most value.

items.stem: Which TWO conditions tend to make a competitive advantage sustainable rather than temporary? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Distinctive capabilities that competitors cannot easily imitate
Isolating mechanisms such as scale economies or switching costs
options.rationale: Correct: isolating mechanisms slow erosion of advantage.

options.text: A current price lower than every rival
options.rationale: A price lead is easily matched and not durable.

options.text: A recent quarter of high profit
options.rationale: High profit alone does not indicate durability.
Spending does not by itself create sustainable advantage.

items.stem: A business is highly profitable yet its industry has low entry barriers and many substitutes. What is the most defensible strategic interpretation?

options.text: Its profit may be vulnerable because industry structure offers weak protection
options.rationale: Correct: weak structure means current profit is at risk without firm-specific advantage.

options.text: Its profit proves it has a sustainable advantage
Industry structure is irrelevant to profitability

items.explanation: Correct: weak structure means current profit is at risk without firm-specific advantage.
